text.textPath: L1 · CLIENTS · ESAF FACADE · SDK · CLI

g.text: Consumer: Python with the ESAF facade
A Python session next to the Factory API (the aif-138 walkthrough), or the lifecycle
Calls one ESAF scenario method. Calling it is the approval; it gets a job
azurefactory Python package: esaf facade over AzureFactoryClient (purple
Thin clients. The esaf facade prepares the review, checks it and confirms it
in one call, then returns an EsafJob. No deployment logic.
src/catalog_runtime.py · loopback on the API host
Owns every decision: catalog, reviews, consent. For PROJECT it only writes
the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's pipeline: 13-24 s
Does the work: networking and services, then AI Foundry, as separate az
deployment steps. 24-52 min per PROJECT run, one wall clock for L3, L4
01-foundation ... 11-integration) and bicep/scripts, at the pinned purple commit
Infrastructure as code the pipeline deploys, plus the scripts it runs around
it. Its time is inside the pipeline's wall clock.
management.azure.com: deployments, resource groups, resources, role
The only layer that changes Azure: networks, private endpoints, DNS, AI
Foundry. Its time is inside the pipeline's wall clock.
Where the time goes: minutes per run, by layer
Measured runs on aif-138, stacked by layer: L2 = job created to GitHub run created (Scenario 5: prepare), L3-L5 = the pipeline split by its
step times (R4). Consumer and L1 take seconds. Worker = the factory-lifecycle worker route.
PROJECT path (API-2-Pipelines): Consumer > L1 esaf > L2 writes the configuration and starts the run (13-24 s) > L3 infra-project pipeline > L4 Bicep > L5 (24-52 min)
Worker path (scale-set enroll): L2 freezes a deployment plan (2 min 18 s) > L3 factory-lifecycle worker > L4 Bicep > L5 (10.1 min)
Colours mark the layers, in the rings and in the chart bars: blue Consumer, green L1 Clients, pink L2 Factory REST API, purple L3 Pipelines, orange L4 Bicep +
pipeline-called scripts, red L5 Azure Resource Manager.
